evidence: Runs of the project's one-dimensional lake model on one climate model's 3-day means at T21, made linear in time, as the cold waters study runs its lake: no lake or sea like these has been measured. A lake far above or below its cell's mean ground takes the cell's air along the land's mean lapse rate. A column stands for the surface water a river draws from its lake and for the sea beside the mouth; neither feels the other, and the sea column is 40 m of a sea hundreds of metres deep, so its floor gives the coldest water the nights' mixing makes there.
reading_rule: Temperatures in C, depths in m. columns[key] gives each distinct column: its model cell, whether that cell is water in the design years' run, its level and the lift above the cell's mean ground, its depth, and its surface's and floor's temperatures after two years' spin-up. rivers[sea] lists, in mouths.json's order, each river's lake column and sea column, and whether each stands on a cell of its own kind (land for a lake, water for a sea). The series are on the research drive under river-oxygen/columns/, one .npz for each column: profile_t holds the temperature of each layer (layer_top_m to layer_bottom_m) every sixth step, and surface_t, bottom_t and mixed_depth every step.
